sections.content: Spanish often presents health information without naming a specific person responsible for an action. Impersonal se is common for general recommendations, while se + third-person verb can describe actions or processes whose agent is not important. These structures are frequent in medical information, notices and public guidance.

items.spanish: Se recomienda beber suficiente agua durante el día.
items.english: It is recommended to drink enough water during the day.

items.spanish: Se deben evitar los alimentos que contienen demasiado azúcar.
items.english: Foods containing too much sugar should be avoided.

items.spanish: En esta clínica se ofrecen consultas gratuitas los viernes.
items.english: Free consultations are offered at this clinic on Fridays.

items.spanish: Para mejorar el descanso, se puede reducir el uso del teléfono por la noche.
items.english: To improve sleep, phone use can be reduced at night.

sections.content: With impersonal se, the verb is normally singular when there is no specific grammatical subject. In passive-like se constructions, the verb agrees with the noun: se ofrece una consulta, se ofrecen consultas.
